title.zh: 卷四十四 列傳第十四 鄭袤 李胤 盧欽 華表 石鑒 溫羨
title.en: Volume 44 Biographies 14: Zheng Mao; Li Yin; Lu Qin; Hua Biao; Shi Jian; Wen Xian
title.raw: 卷四十四 列傳第十四 鄭袤 李胤 盧欽 華表 石鑒 溫羨 Volume 44 Biographies 14: Zheng Mao; Li Yin; Lu Qin; Hua Biao; Shi Jian; Wen Xian

sentences.zh: 鄭袤，字林叔，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Mao, courtesy name Linshu, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao, courtesy name Linshu, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖眾，漢大司農。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Zhong was Han Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Zheng Zhong had served the Han as grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 父泰，揚州刺史，有高名。

translations.literal: His father Tai was Inspector of Yang Province and had high repute.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tai had been inspector of Yang Province and enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 袤少孤，早有識鑒。

translations.literal: Mao in youth was orphaned, early had judgment and insight.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while young yet showed early discernment.

sentences.zh: 荀攸見之曰：「鄭公業為不亡矣。

translations.literal: Xun You seeing him said, "Lord Zheng Gongye is not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said of him, "Zheng Gongye's line will not die out."

sentences.zh: 」隨叔父渾避難江東。

translations.literal: " He followed his uncle Hun to flee trouble east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his uncle Zheng Hun into exile east of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 時華歆為豫章太守，渾往依之，歆素與泰善，撫養袤如己子。

translations.literal: At the time Hua Xin was governor of Yuzhang; Hun went to rely on him; Xin plain was on good terms with Tai, and reared Mao like his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin was then governor of Yuzhang; Zheng Hun went to him for shelter, and because Xin had long been friendly with Tai he raised Mao as his own child.

sentences.zh: 年十七，乃還鄉里。

translations.literal: His years seventeen, then he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he returned to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 性清正。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature pure and upright.

sentences.zh: 時濟陰魏諷為相國掾，名重當世，袤同郡任覽與結交。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Feng of Jiyin was aide to the chancellor of state, his name weighty in the age; Mao's same-commandery Ren Lan befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Feng of Jiyin was then an aide in the chancellery, a man of great fame, and Ren Lan of Mao's commandery became his friend.

sentences.zh: 袤以諷奸雄，終必為禍，勸覽遠之。

translations.literal: Mao because Feng was a treacherous hero, in the end would surely become disaster, urged Lan to distance from him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao judged Feng a dangerous schemer who would bring ruin in the end and urged Ren Lan to break with him.

sentences.zh: 及諷敗，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: When Feng was defeated, those who discussed praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng fell, commentators praised Mao's foresight.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉作亂，景帝自出征之，百官祖送於城東，袤疾病不任會。

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian made rebellion; Prince Jing himself went out to campaign against him; the hundred officials performed the road sacrifice seeing-off east of the wall; Mao was ill in sickness and could not bear to attend the meeting.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian rose in revolt, Prince Jing took the field in person; officials gathered east of the city for the farewell rites, but Mao was too ill to attend.

sentences.zh: 帝謂中領軍王肅曰：「唯不見鄭光祿為恨。

translations.literal: The prince said to Central Army Commander Wang Su, "Only not seeing Zheng Guanglu is regret.
translations.idiomatic: The prince told Central Army Commander Wang Su, "My only regret is that Zheng Guanglu is not here."

sentences.zh: 」肅以語袤，袤自輿追帝，及於近道。

translations.literal: " Su told Mao; Mao himself in a litter pursued the prince and caught him on the near road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su told Mao, who had himself carried in a litter until he overtook the prince on the road.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「故知侯生必來也。

translations.literal: The prince laughed and said, "So I knew Lord Hou would surely come.
translations.idiomatic: The prince laughed and said, "I knew our Hou Ying would turn up."

sentences.zh: 」遂與袤共載，曰：「計將何先？

translations.literal: " Then together with Mao he shared a carriage, saying, "In planning, what first?
translations.idiomatic: He had Mao ride with him and asked, "What should be our first move?"

sentences.zh: 」袤曰：「昔與儉俱為台郎，特所知悉。

translations.literal: " Mao said, "Formerly with Jian together I was a terrace gentleman; especially I know him thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Mao replied, "I served with Jian as a terrace gentleman and know him well."

sentences.zh: 其人好謀而不達事情，自昔建勳幽州，志望無限。

translations.literal: That man loves plotting yet does not comprehend affairs; from the time he first built merit in You Province, his aims and hopes have been limitless.
translations.idiomatic: He loves schemes but misreads the situation; since he first won glory in You Province his ambitions have known no bound.

sentences.zh: 文欽勇而無算。

translations.literal: Wen Qin is brave yet without calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin is brave but reckless.

sentences.zh: 今大軍出其不意，江、淮之卒銳而不能固，深溝高壘以挫其氣，此亞夫之長也。

translations.literal: Now the great army goes out where they do not expect; Jiang and Huai's troops are keen yet cannot hold firm; deep moats and high walls to blunt their qi — this is Zhou Yafu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Strike before they expect it; the Jiang and Huai troops are eager but cannot hold a line—dig deep moats and raise high walls to break their spirit, as Zhou Yafu would have done."

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: " The prince praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The prince approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 轉太常。

translations.literal: He was transferred Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公議立明堂辟雍，精選博士，袤舉劉毅、劉寔、程咸、庾峻，後並至公輔大位。

translations.literal: Duke of Gaoguixiang discussed establishing Bright Hall and Ring Moat, finely selecting erudites; Mao raised Liu Yi, Liu Shi, Cheng Xian, Yu Jun — later all reached great office among the three councillors.
translations.idiomatic: When the duke of Gaoguixiang debated founding the Bright Hall and ring moat and chose erudits with care, Mao nominated Liu Yi, Liu Shi, Cheng Xian, and Yu Jun, all of whom later rose to the highest councils.

sentences.zh: 及常道鄉公立，與議定策，進封安城鄉侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the duke of Changdaoxiang was established, he participated in deliberating fixing the policy; advanced enfeoffment as marquis of Ancheng village, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the duke of Changdaoxiang was enthroned, Mao joined in framing the succession plan and was promoted to marquis of Ancheng township with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 景元初，疾病失明，屢乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyuan, illness made him lose sight; repeatedly he begged his bones; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyuan era illness blinded him; he repeatedly asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand master of splendid carriage.

sentences.zh: 五等初建，封密陵伯。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were first established, he was enfeoffed earl of Miling.
translations.idiomatic: When the five noble ranks were first instituted he was enfeoffed as earl of Miling.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ascended the steps; he advanced in noble rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Mao's rank rose to marquis.

sentences.zh: 雖寢疾十餘年，而時賢並相推薦。

translations.literal: Although bed-ill more than ten years, yet men of worth of the time together recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was bedridden for more than ten years, leading men kept recommending him for office.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，詔曰：「光祿密陵侯袤，履行純正，守道沖粹，退有清和之風，進有素絲之節，宜登三階之曜，補袞職之闕。

translations.literal: In Taishi an edict said, "Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, Marquis of Miling Mao, in conduct and practice is pure and straight, keeps the Way empty and pure; in withdrawal has clear and harmonious wind, in advance has plain silk's integrity; ought to ascend the three steps' radiance, fill the ducal robe office's gap.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi an edict declared, "Grand Master of Splendid Carriage and Marquis of Miling Zheng Mao walks a path of utter integrity, cleaves to the Way in humble purity, shows the gentle clarity of a recluse in private and the unstained white silk of a minister in public; he should mount the three steps of honor and fill a place among the highest councillors."

sentences.zh: 今以袤為司空。

translations.literal: Now we appoint Mao Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: We hereby appoint Mao minister of works."

sentences.zh: 」天子臨軒，遣五官中郎將國坦就第拜授。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven approached the gallery and sent Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes Guo Tan to his mansion to invest the office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appeared above the gallery and sent Guo Tan, gentleman of the household for all purposes, to Mao's house to confer the seal.

sentences.zh: 袤前後辭讓，遣息稱上送印綬，至於十數。

translations.literal: Mao before and after declined yielding, sending his son Cheng upward to deliver seals and ribbons, reaching more than ten times.
translations.idiomatic: Mao declined again and again, sending his son Cheng to return the seals more than ten times.

sentences.zh: 謂坦曰：「魏以徐景山為司空，吾時為侍中，受詔譬旨。

translations.literal: He said to Tan, "Wei appointed Xu Jingshan Minister of Works; I at the time was Palace Attendant, received the edict to explain the intent.
translations.idiomatic: He told Guo Tan, "When Wei named Xu Miao minister of works, I was palace attendant and carried the edict explaining its intent."

sentences.zh: 徐公語吾曰：'三公當上應天心，苟非其人，實傷和氣，不敢以垂死之年，累辱朝廷也。

translations.literal: Lord Xu said to me, 'The Three Dukes ought above to answer Heaven's mind; if indeed not that man, it truly injures harmonious qi; I dare not, with years hanging toward death, repeatedly shame the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xu told me, "The Three Dukes must mirror Heaven's will; the wrong man in office harms the harmony of the realm; I will not burden the court with my dying breath."

sentences.zh: '終於不就。

translations.literal: ' In the end he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused the post."

sentences.zh: 遵大雅君子之跡，可不務乎！

translations.literal: To follow the traces of the great-ya gentleman — can it not be urgently pursued!
translations.idiomatic: Ought we not follow the example of such a gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 」固辭，久之見許，以侯就第，拜儀同三司，置舍人官騎，賜床帳簟褥、錢五十萬。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined; after a long time he was permitted, as marquis went to mansion, was appointed with parity of the Three Dukes, established householders and official riders, bestowed bed curtains, bamboo mats, bedding, and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He held firm until the court relented; he retired to his mansion as a marquis with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, household attendants and mounted escort, and gifts of bed-curtains, mats, bedding, and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 九年薨，時年八十五。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; at the time his years were eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the era, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝於東堂發哀，賜秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬、絹布各百匹，以供喪事。

translations.literal: The emperor at the Eastern Hall expressed mourning, bestowed secret coffin gear, one set court robes, one suit clothes, three hundred thousand cash, silk and cloth each one hundred bolts, to supply the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at the Eastern Hall and sent a private burial outfit, court robes, a suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, and a hundred bolts each of silk and cloth for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Yuan, "Primal."

sentences.zh: 有子六人，長子默嗣，次質、舒、詡、稱、予，位並列卿。

translations.literal: He had six sons; the eldest son Mo succeeded; next Zhi, Shu, Xu, Cheng, Yu — their offices all reached the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: the heir Mo, then Zhi, Shu, Xu, Cheng, and Yu, all of whom rose to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 默字思元。

translations.literal: Mo, courtesy name Siyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's courtesy name was Siyuan.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，考核舊文，刪省浮穢。

translations.literal: He first rose as Secretariat gentleman, examined and verified old texts, deleted and reduced floating filth.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a gentleman of the palace secretariat, reviewing old documents and cutting away the worthless dross.

sentences.zh: 中書令虞松謂曰：「而今而後，硃紫別矣。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Yu Song said to him, "From now onward, vermilion and purple are divided.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song, director of the palace secretariat, told him, "From this day vermilion and purple will not be confused."

sentences.zh: 」轉尚書考功郎，專典伐蜀事，封關內侯，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: " He was transferred Merit Evaluation gentleman of the Masters of Writing, solely in charge of the campaign against Shu affairs, enfeoffed marquis within the passes, promoted chief clerk on the left of the minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: He was named merit-evaluation gentleman of the masters of writing with sole charge of the Shu campaign, enfeoffed as marquis within the passes, then promoted chief clerk on the left of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，與太原郭奕俱為中庶子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, together with Guo Yi of Taiyuan he both was Household Gentleman to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Mo and Guo Yi of Taiyuan were both named household gentlemen to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以太子官屬宜稱陪臣。

translations.literal: The court held that the heir apparent's official subordinates ought to be called attendant ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that the heir apparent's staff should style themselves attendant ministers to the throne.

sentences.zh: 默上言：「皇太子體皇極之尊，無私於天下。

translations.literal: Mo submitted words: "The imperial heir apparent embodies the imperial extreme's honor; he has no partiality toward the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized: "The crown prince embodies the supremacy of the throne and holds the empire without private favor."

sentences.zh: 宮臣皆受命天朝，不得同之籓國。

translations.literal: Palace ministers all receive mandate from the heavenly court; they cannot be treated the same as fief states.
translations.idiomatic: His household officers receive their mandate from the imperial court and cannot be classed with vassal princes' retainers."

sentences.zh: 」事遂施行。

translations.literal: " The matter then was put in practice.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 出為東郡太守，值歲荒人饑，默輒開倉振給，乃舍都亭，自表待罪。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Dong commandery; it met a year of famine and people hungered; Mo then opened granaries to relieve and supply, then left the metropolitan post station, self-memorialized awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Dong commandery he faced famine; he opened the granaries for relief, then moved out of the official residence and memorialized himself for punishment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉默憂國，詔書褒歎，比之汲黯。

translations.literal: The court praised Mo's worrying for the state; an edict praised and sighed, comparing him to Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his concern for the state and issued an edict comparing him to Ji An of Han.

sentences.zh: 班告天下，若郡縣有此比者，皆聽出給。

translations.literal: It was promulgated to inform the realm; if commanderies and counties have such cases, all are permitted to go out and supply.
translations.idiomatic: The decree was published empire-wide: wherever famine struck, magistrates might open the granaries on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以貴公子當品，鄉里莫敢與為輩，求之州內，於是十二郡中正僉共舉默。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor because a noble heir-son was being ranked, in the village none dared be his peer; seeking within the province, thereupon the twelve commanderies' middle appraisers together raised Mo.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor as a princely heir was being graded for office, no one in his village would rank alongside him, so the province was searched and the twelve commandery appraisers jointly nominated Mo.

sentences.zh: 文帝與袤書曰：「小兒得廁賢子之流，愧有竅賢之累。

translations.literal: Prince Wen wrote Mao a letter, saying, "The little boy gets to rank among your worthy sons' flow; ashamed to have the flaw of unworthy among worthies' burden.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen wrote to Mao, "My son is honored to stand among your worthy sons; I blush that his mediocrity burdens their company."

sentences.zh: 」及武帝出祀南郊，詔使默驂乘，因謂默曰：「卿知何以得驂乘乎？

translations.literal: " When Emperor Wu went out to sacrifice at the southern suburb, an edict ordered Mo to ride tandem in the carriage, and thereby said to Mo, "Do you know by what you got to ride tandem?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Wu rode to sacrifice at the southern suburb, he had Mo take the place of honor beside him in the chariot and asked, "Do you know why you are here?"

sentences.zh: 昔州裏舉卿相輩，常愧有累清談。

translations.literal: Formerly the province and village raised you as his peer; I always was ashamed it burdened pure discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When the province ranked you his equal, I always feared it would taint pure conversation."

sentences.zh: 」遂問政事，對曰：「勸穡務農，為國之基。

translations.literal: " Then he asked government affairs; he replied, saying, "Urging harvest and devoting to farming is the state's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked his views on government. Mo replied, "Encourage farming and the harvest—that is the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 選人得才，濟世之道。

translations.literal: Selecting men and obtaining talent is the way to aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men of talent—that is how to serve the age.

sentences.zh: 居官久職，政事之宜。

translations.literal: Dwelling in office long in post is government affairs' fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Let officials serve long in one post—that suits good government.

sentences.zh: 明慎黜陟，勸戒之由。

translations.literal: Bright and careful demotions and promotions are the source of exhortation and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Promote and demote with clear care—that is how to teach and warn.

sentences.zh: 崇尚儒素，化導之本。

translations.literal: Esteeming and honoring Confucian plainness is transformation and guidance's root.
translations.idiomatic: Honor plain Confucian virtue—that is the root of moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 如此而已矣。

translations.literal: Like this only — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing more than that."

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his answer.

sentences.zh: 後以父喪去官，尋起為廷尉。

translations.literal: Later because of father's mourning he left office; shortly he rose as Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned for his father's mourning, then was recalled as director of justice.

sentences.zh: 是時鬲令袁毅坐交通貨賂，大興刑獄。

translations.literal: At this time the Ge magistrate Yuan Yi sat guilty of trafficking and bribes; greatly they raised punishments and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Yi, magistrate of Ge, was impeached for bribery and a vast criminal investigation followed.

sentences.zh: 在朝多見引逮，唯默兄弟以潔慎不染其流。

translations.literal: Those at court mostly were led and seized; only Mo and his brothers by purity and care did not dye in that current.
translations.idiomatic: Most courtiers were dragged into the net, but Mo and his brothers stayed clean and were never touched.

sentences.zh: 遷太常。

translations.literal: He was promoted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時僕射山濤欲舉一親親為博士，謂默曰：「卿似尹翁歸，令吾不敢復言。

translations.literal: At the time Supervisor Shan Tao wished to raise one close kin as erudite, and said to Mo, "You resemble Yin Wenggui — it makes me dare not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice-Director Shan Tao wanted to nominate a kinsman as erudite, he told Mo, "You are another Yin Wenggui—you leave me speechless."

sentences.zh: 」默為人敦重，柔而能整，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " Mo as a man was thick and weighty, soft yet able to be strict — all was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was grave and steady, gentle yet firm—always in this vein.

sentences.zh: 及齊王攸當之國，下禮官議崇錫典制。

translations.literal: When Prince You of Qi was about to go to his state, he ordered ritual officials to deliberate honors and gifts canonical regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince You of Qi was sent to his fief, the court ordered ritual officers to debate the honors and gifts due him.

sentences.zh: 博士祭酒曹志等並立異議，默容過其事，坐免。

translations.literal: Libationer Cao Zhi and others together set up divergent opinions; Mo tolerated and passed over the affair; sitting, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi the libationer and others dissented; Mo let the matter pass and was dismissed for it.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named grand herald.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，舊制，既葬還職，默自陳懇至，久而見許。

translations.literal: He encountered mother's mourning; by old regulation, after burial return to office; Mo self-stated earnestness to the utmost; after a long time he was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the old rule required return to duty after burial, but Mo pleaded with such persistence that the court eventually let him observe the full mourning.

sentences.zh: 遂改法定令，聽大臣終喪，自默始也。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed law and fixed decree, hearing great ministers complete mourning — from Mo it began.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes were then revised to allow great ministers to finish mourning—beginning with Mo.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為大司農，轉光祿勳。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Grand Minister of Agriculture, transferred Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as grand minister of agriculture, then as master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 默子球

translations.literal: Mo's son Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Mo had a son named Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球字子瑜。

translations.literal: Qiu, courtesy name Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's courtesy name was Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 少辟宰府，入侍二宮。

translations.literal: In youth he was summoned to the chief's bureau, entered to attend the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was summoned to the minister's office and entered service in the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 成都王為大將軍，起義討趙王倫，球自頓丘太守為右長史，以功封平壽公。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengdu was Grand General, raised righteousness to punish Prince of Zhao Lun; Qiu from Dunqiu governor became Right Chief Clerk; by merit he was enfeoffed duke of Pingshou.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Chengdu served as grand general and raised troops against Sima Lun, prince of Zhao, Qiu moved from governor of Dunqiu to chief clerk on the right and was enfeoffed as duke of Pingshou for his merit.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、尚書、散騎常侍、中護軍、尚書右僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: By accumulated transfers he became Palace Attendant, Minister of the Secretariat, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Central Protector of the Army, Right Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently heading the Personnel Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through palace attendant, minister of the secretariat, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, central protector of the army, and right vice-director of the masters of writing while heading the personnel ministry.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年卒，追贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰元。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongjia he died; posthumously he was given Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his posthumous name was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongjia and was posthumously named grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon with the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 球弟豫，永嘉末為尚書。

translations.literal: Qiu's younger brother Yu, at the end of Yongjia was Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's younger brother Yu became a minister of the secretariat late in the Yongjia era.

sentences.zh: 李胤，字宣伯，遼東襄平人也。

translations.literal: Li Yin, courtesy name Xuanbo, was a man of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin, courtesy name Xuanbo, came from Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祖敏，漢河內太守，去官還鄉里，遼東太守公孫度欲強用之，敏乘輕舟浮滄海，莫知所終。

translations.literal: His grandfather Min was Han governor of Henei; leaving office he returned to his home village; Liaodong Governor Gongsun Du wished forcibly to use him; Min rode a light boat floating the deep sea — none knows his end.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Min had been governor of Henei under the Han; he resigned and went home, but Gongsun Du, governor of Liaodong, meant to force him into service, so Min fled in a light boat across the sea and was never heard from again.

sentences.zh: 胤父信追求積年，浮海出塞，竟無所見，欲行喪制服，則疑父尚存，情若居喪而不聘娶。

translations.literal: Yin's father Xin pursued seeking accumulated years, floated the sea out beyond the passes, in the end saw nothing; wishing to practice mourning dress system, then doubted the father still lived; his feeling was as if dwelling in mourning yet did not take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's father Xin searched for years, sailing beyond the frontier, and found no trace; he could not don full mourning while his father might still live, yet he lived as a mourner and would not marry.

sentences.zh: 後有鄰居故人與其父同年者亡，因行喪制服。

translations.literal: Later a neighbor old friend who was the same birth year as his father died; thereby he practiced mourning dress system.
translations.idiomatic: When an old neighbor who had shared his father's birth year died, Xin at last put on mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 燕國徐邈與之同州裏，以不孝莫大於無後，勸使娶妻。

translations.literal: Xu Miao of Yan state was with him same village in the commandery; holding that among unfilial acts none is greater than having no posterity, urged him to take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao of Yan, a townsman, urged him to marry, arguing that the worst unfilial act was to leave no heir.

sentences.zh: 既生胤，遂絕房室，恆如居喪禮，不堪其憂，數年而卒。

translations.literal: After Yin was born, then he cut off bedchamber, always as if dwelling in mourning rites; he could not bear the grief; in several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin was born he left his wife's bed for good and lived as if in perpetual mourning until grief wore him out and he died within a few years.

sentences.zh: 胤既幼孤，母又改行，有識之後，降食哀戚，亦以喪禮自居。

translations.literal: Yin was then young orphaned; his mother again changed conduct; after he had understanding, he reduced food in grief and sorrow, also took mourning rites as his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was orphaned young; his mother remarried badly, and once he could reason he ate less in grief and kept himself under mourning discipline.

sentences.zh: 又以祖不知存亡，設木主以事之。

translations.literal: Again because his grandfather was not known alive or dead, he set a wooden tablet to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his grandfather's fate was unknown, he set up a spirit tablet and made offerings.

sentences.zh: 由是以孝聞。

translations.literal: Thereby by filial piety he was heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he became known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 容貌質素，頹然若不足者，而知度沈邃，言必有則。

translations.literal: His appearance was plain and simple, drooping as if insufficient; yet his knowledge and measure were deep and remote, speech always had rule.
translations.idiomatic: He looked plain and almost frail, yet his judgment ran deep and every word carried weight.

sentences.zh: 初仕郡上計掾，州辟部從事、治中，舉孝廉，參鎮北軍事。

translations.literal: He first served the commandery as chief clerk on the accounts mission; the province summoned him section attendant and staff supervisor; he was raised Filial and Incorrupt; he joined Pacify-the-North Army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commandery accounts clerk, was summoned to the province as section attendant and staff supervisor, nominated Filial and Incorrupt, and joined the staff of the army that pacified the north.

sentences.zh: 遷樂平侯相，政尚清簡。

translations.literal: He was transferred Marquis of Leping's chancellor; his government esteemed clarity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He became chancellor to the marquis of Leping and governed with austere simplicity.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書郎，遷中護軍司馬、吏部郎，銓綜廉平。

translations.literal: He entered as Secretariat gentleman, was promoted Central Protector of the Army marshal, Personnel Ministry gentleman; in ranking and judging he was honest and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the masters of writing, rose to marshal under the central protector of the army and gentleman in the personnel ministry, and ranked candidates with incorrupt fairness.

sentences.zh: 賜爵關中侯，出補安豐太守。

translations.literal: He was bestowed noble rank marquis within the passes, went out to fill Anfeng governor.
translations.idiomatic: He received the rank of marquis within the passes and was sent out as governor of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 文帝引為大將軍從事中郎，遷御史中丞，恭恪直繩，百官憚之。

translations.literal: Prince Wen summoned him as aide to the grand general, then promoted him to palace assistant secretary; he was reverent, scrupulous, and strict as a plumb line, and the bureaucracy feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as aide to the grand general, he rose to palace assistant secretary; his grave integrity and uncompromising standards awed every office.

sentences.zh: 伐蜀之役，為西中郎將、督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Shu he served as general of the central guard on the west and supervised military affairs within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu expedition he was named general of the central guard on the west with command of all forces in the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 後為河南尹，封廣陸伯。

translations.literal: Later he became intendant of Henan and was enfeoffed as earl of Guanglu.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as intendant of Henan and received the title earl of Guanglu.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，拜尚書，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was appointed minister of the masters of writing and advanced in noble rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he became a minister of the masters of writing and his noble rank rose to marquis.

sentences.zh: 胤奏以為：「古者三公坐而論道，內參六官之事，外與六卿之教，或處三槐，兼聽獄訟，稽疑之典，謀及卿士。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized: "In antiquity the three dukes sat to discuss the Way; within they joined the six palaces’ affairs, without they matched the six ministers’ instruction; sometimes they sat beneath the three locusts, concurrently hearing lawsuits and doubtful cases, consulting the high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted: "The three ancient dukes sat in council on the Way, joined the six palaces within and matched the six ministers without, heard cases beneath the court locusts, and took doubtful matters to the high ministers."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德欽明，垂心萬機，猥發明詔，儀刑古式，雖唐、虞疇諮，周文翼翼，無以加也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s sagely virtue is reverent and bright; you bend your mind to the myriad threads of rule. Humbly you have issued a clarifying edict to model yourself on ancient forms—though Yao and Shun sought counsel far and wide, and King Wen was ever vigilant, none could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty’s luminous virtue attends to every detail of government; this edict, humbly issued to mirror antiquity, matches even Yao, Shun, and the vigilant King Wen."

sentences.zh: 自今以往，國有大政，可親延群公，詢納讜言。

translations.literal: From this time forward, whenever the state faces great policy, you may personally extend audience to the high ministers and gather candid counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, on great affairs of state, summon the dukes in person and draw in forthright advice."

sentences.zh: 其軍國所疑，延詣省中，使侍中、尚書諮論所宜。

translations.literal: Where military and civil matters raise doubt, prolong consultation in the palace secretariat and let palace attendants and ministers debate what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When civil and military questions remain unsettled, hold prolonged discussion in the secretariat with palace attendants and ministers."

sentences.zh: 若有疾病，不任覲會，臨時遣侍臣訊訪。

translations.literal: If illness prevents attendance at court, dispatch attendants at once to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: If someone is too ill for assembly, send palace attendants to consult him."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書僕射，尋轉太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was promoted minister of personnel and vice-director of the masters of writing, then shortly became junior tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of personnel and vice-director of the masters of writing, then soon junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔以胤忠允高亮，有匪躬之節，使領司隸校尉。

translations.literal: An edict, because Yin was loyal, even-tempered, and high-minded with the integrity of one who does not spare himself, ordered him to act as metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him metropolitan commandant for his loyal, even temper and selfless integrity.

sentences.zh: 胤屢自表讓，忝傅儲宮，不宜兼監司之官。

translations.literal: Yin repeatedly memorialized to decline, ashamed to tutor the heir while also holding the censor’s surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: Yin begged off again and again: tutoring the heir should not be combined with the metropolitan command."

sentences.zh: 武帝以二職並須忠賢，故每不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu held that both posts required loyal worthies, so each time he refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that both offices demanded loyal talent and would not release him.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，皇太子出居東宮，帝以司錄事任峻重，而少傅有旦夕輔導之務，胤素羸，不宜久勞之，轉拜侍中，加特進。

translations.literal: Early in Xianning the crown prince moved to the eastern palace; the emperor deemed the metropolitan commandant’s burden too heavy for Yin’s frailty alongside the junior tutor’s daily instruction, so he transferred him to palace attendant with the title specially advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning, when the crown prince entered the eastern palace, the emperor thought the metropolitan post too crushing for Yin’s frail health beside the tutor’s daily duties, and named him palace attendant with the title specially advanced instead.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書令，侍中、特進如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted director of the masters of writing, keeping palace attendant and specially advanced as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became director of the masters of writing while retaining palace attendant and specially advanced.

sentences.zh: 胤雖曆職內外，而家至貧儉，兒病無以市藥。

translations.literal: Though Yin served in and out of court, his household was utterly poor; when a son fell ill he could not buy medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Despite long service, his family remained destitute; when his son fell ill he had no money for drugs.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he granted one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 其後帝以司徒舊丞相之職，詔以胤為司徒。

translations.literal: Later the emperor, because the minister of education had been the old chancellor’s office, appointed Yin minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Later, recalling that the minister of education had once been the chancellor’s role, the emperor named Yin to that post.

sentences.zh: 在位五年，簡亮持重，稱為任職。

translations.literal: During five years in office he was concise, bright, and steady, and was praised as equal to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he governed with terse clarity and weight and was reckoned fully competent.

sentences.zh: 以吳會初平，大臣多有勳勞，宜有登進，乃上疏遜位。

translations.literal: Because Wu region had just been pacified and many great ministers merited promotion, he submitted a memorial yielding his place.
translations.idiomatic: With the southeast newly pacified and many ministers owed reward, he offered to step down.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，遣侍中宣旨，優詔敦諭，絕其章表。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen; he sent a palace attendant to proclaim intent, answered with a gracious ed urging him on, and cut off further memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, sent a palace attendant with a gracious edict, and barred further resignations.

sentences.zh: 胤不得已，起視事。

translations.literal: Yin had no choice but to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had to return to his desk.

sentences.zh: 太康三年薨，詔遣御史持節監喪致祠，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Taikang; an edict sent a censor with staff to oversee the rites and sacrifices, with posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taikang; a censor with credential staff oversaw his obsequies and he received the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 皇太子命舍人王贊誄之，文義甚美。

translations.literal: The crown prince ordered his householder Wang Zan to compose a dirge; the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had Wang Zan compose his dirge in beautiful prose.

sentences.zh: 帝后思胤清節，詔曰：「故司徒李胤，太常彭灌，並履忠清儉，身沒，家無餘積，賜胤家錢二百萬、穀千斛，灌家半之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor remembered Yin’s purity and issued an edict: "The late minister of education Li Yin and Minister of Ceremonies Peng Guan both walked in loyalty, purity, and frugality; when they died their houses held no surplus. Grant two million cash and a thousand hu of grain to Yin’s family, half that to Guan’s.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor recalled Yin’s integrity and decreed: "The late Li Yin and Peng Guan, minister of ceremonies, died poor in loyal service; give two million cash and a thousand hu of grain to Yin’s heirs, half to Guan’s."

sentences.zh: 」三子，固、真長、修。

translations.literal: " He had three sons: Gu, Zhenchang, and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Gu, Zhenchang, and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 固字萬基，散騎郎，先胤卒，固子志嗣爵。

translations.literal: Gu, courtesy name Wanji, was a cavalier gentleman; he predeceased Yin, and his son Zhi inherited the noble title.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, courtesy name Wanji, served as cavalier gentleman, died before his father, and his son Zhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 志字彥道，歷位散騎侍郎、建威將軍、陽平太守。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Yandao, held posts as cavalier gentleman at the palace, general who establishes might, and governor of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Yandao, rose through cavalier gentleman at the palace, general who establishes might, and governor of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 真長位至太僕卿。

translations.literal: Zhenchang rose to minister of the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenchang reached minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 修黃門侍郎、太弟中庶子。

translations.literal: Xiu was palace attendant at the yellow gates and household gentleman to the imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu served as palace attendant at the yellow gates and household gentleman to the heir-designate.

sentences.zh: 盧欽，字子若，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qin, courtesy name Ziruo, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin, courtesy name Ziruo, came from Zhuo in Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖植，漢侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi was a Han palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi had been a palace attendant under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父毓，魏司空。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Wei minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had been minister of works under Wei.

sentences.zh: 世以儒業顯。

translations.literal: For generations the family was eminent in Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long won fame for Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 欽清淡有遠識，篤志經史，舉孝廉，不行，魏大將軍曹爽辟為掾。

translations.literal: Qin was clear, spare, and far-sighted, devoted to the classics and histories; he was nominated Filial and Incorrupt but did not go, and Wei’s grand general Cao Shuang summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was sober, detached, and long-sighted, steeped in the classics and histories; nominated Filial and Incorrupt, he stayed home until Cao Shuang summoned him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 爽弟嘗有所屬請，欽白爽子弟不宜干犯法度，爽深納之，而罰其弟。

translations.literal: Once Shuang’s younger brother made a private request; Qin told Shuang that his kin should not break the law, Shuang deeply accepted this, and punished his brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang’s brother sought a private favor, Qin warned that kinsmen must not violate the statutes; Shuang agreed and punished his brother.

sentences.zh: 除尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was named gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，免官。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang fell, Qin lost his post.

sentences.zh: 後為侍御史，襲父爵大利亭侯，累遷琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Later he became attendant censor, inherited his father’s title as marquis of Dali village, and rose to governor of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as attendant censor, inherited the marquisate of Dali village, and became governor of Langye.

sentences.zh: 宣帝為太傅，辟從事中郎，出為陽平太守，遷淮北都督、伏波將軍，甚有稱績。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was grand tutor, he summoned Qin as an aide, then sent him out as governor of Yangping, promoted him area commander north of the Huai and general who crosses the waves, with a strong reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: As grand tutor, Emperor Xuan made him an aide, then governor of Yangping, then area commander north of the Huai and general who crosses the waves, earning high praise.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍、大司農，遷吏部尚書，進封大梁侯。

translations.literal: He was summoned as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and grand minister of agriculture, promoted minister of personnel, and advanced to marquis of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and grand minister of agriculture, then minister of personnel, and enfeoffed as marquis of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，以為都督沔北諸軍事、平南將軍、假節，給追鋒軺臥車各一乘、第二駙馬二乘、騎具刀器、禦府人馬鎧等，及錢三十萬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, he made Qin area commander of all forces north of the Mian, general who pacifies the south, with credential staff, granting swift escort carts, sleeping carts, one each, two second-grade outrider teams, mounted gear and blades, palace armory armor for men and horses, and three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin he was named area commander north of the Han, general who pacifies the south, with credential staff, plus swift carts, sleeping carts, outriders, arms from the palace armory, and three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 欽在鎮寬猛得中，疆埸無虞。

translations.literal: At his post he balanced severity and kindness; the frontier stayed quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In command he mixed lenience and firmness and kept the border untroubled.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書僕射，加侍中、奉車都尉，領吏部。

translations.literal: He entered as vice-director of the masters of writing, added palace attendant and colonel who conducts the carriage, and headed the personnel ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice-director of the masters of writing with palace attendant and colonel who conducts the carriage, heading personnel.

sentences.zh: 以清貧，特賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because he was pure and poor, he was specially granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For his honest poverty the court sent a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 欽舉必以材，稱為廉平。

translations.literal: Qin always promoted by talent and was praised as honest and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He chose men by ability and was called incorrupt and even-handed.

sentences.zh: 浮字子雲，起家太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Fu, courtesy name Ziyun, first rose as household gentleman to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Ziyun, began as household gentleman to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 病疽截手，遂廢。

translations.literal: He suffered a carbuncle and had a hand amputated, and so was crippled.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle cost him a hand and ended his career.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷器重之，以為國子博士、祭酒、秘書監，皆不就。

translations.literal: Yet the court esteemed him, naming him erudite of the imperial academy, libationer, and director of the palace library, posts he never took up.
translations.idiomatic: The court still offered him posts as erudite, libationer of the academy, and director of the palace library, but he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 欽弟珽，字子笏，衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Qin’s younger brother Ting, courtesy name Zihu, was minister of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ting, courtesy name Zihu, served as minister of the guards.

sentences.zh: 珽子志。

translations.literal: Ting’s son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ting’s son was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 珽子志

translations.literal: Ting’s son Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Ting’s son Zhi

sentences.zh: 志字子道，初辟公府掾、尚書郎，出為鄴令。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Zidao, was first summoned as aide in the public bureau and gentleman of the masters of writing, then became magistrate of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Zidao, began as a bureau aide and gentleman of the masters of writing, then magistrate of Ye.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎之鎮鄴也，愛其才量，委以心膂，遂為謀主。

translations.literal: When Prince Ying of Chengdu garrisoned Ye, he loved Zhi’s talent and capacity, entrusted him as heart and loins, and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying of Chengdu held Ye, he prized Zhi’s ability and made him his closest adviser.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏起義，遣使告穎。

translations.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi raised loyal troops and sent envoys to inform Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiong of Qi rose in arms, he notified Ying.

sentences.zh: 穎召志計事，志曰：「趙王無道，肆行篡逆，四海人神，莫不憤怒。

translations.literal: Ying summoned Zhi to plan; Zhi said, "The prince of Zhao is lawless and usurps the throne; men and spirits within the four seas seethe with rage.
translations.idiomatic: Ying called Zhi in council. Zhi said, "Sima Lun is a traitor; every corner of the realm burns with anger."

sentences.zh: 今殿下總率三軍，應期電發，子來之眾，不召自至。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness commands the three hosts; strike at the appointed hour like lightning and the hosts will come without summons.
translations.idiomatic: If you lead the three armies and move like lightning, the armies will flock unbidden."

sentences.zh: 掃夷凶逆，必有征無戰。

translations.literal: You will sweep away the traitors and win without a hard fight.
translations.idiomatic: You will crush the rebels and prevail without a prolonged war."

sentences.zh: 然兵事至重，聖人所慎。

translations.literal: Yet war is the weightiest matter, which sages treat with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Yet war is the gravest thing, which the sages handle with fear."

sentences.zh: 宜旌賢任才，以收時望。

translations.literal: You should signal worthies and employ talent to win the age’s confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Raise banners for worthies and employ talent to secure public trust."

sentences.zh: 」穎深然之，改選上佐，高辟掾屬，以志為諮議參軍，仍補左長史，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: " Ying deeply agreed, changed his senior staff, and widely summoned aides, appointing Zhi army adviser, then chief clerk on the left with sole charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Ying agreed, reshuffled his high staff, and named Zhi army adviser, then chief clerk on the left in charge of all paperwork.

sentences.zh: 穎前鋒都督趙驤為倫所敗，士眾震駭，議者多欲還保朝歌。

translations.literal: Ying’s vanguard commander Zhao Xiang was defeated by Lun; the army was shaken and many wished to fall back on Chaoge.
translations.idiomatic: When vanguard Zhao Xiang lost to Lun, panic spread and many wanted to retreat to Chaoge.

sentences.zh: 志曰：「今我軍失利，敵新得勝，必有輕易陵轢之情，若頓兵不進，三軍畏衄，懼不可用。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Our defeat means the enemy is newly victorious and will despise us; if we halt, the army will fear rout and be useless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "A reverse makes the foe overconfident; if we freeze in place, morale will collapse."

sentences.zh: 且戰何能無勝負，宜更選精兵，星行倍道，出賊不意，此用兵之奇也。

translations.literal: Moreover battle always knows victory and defeat—choose crack troops, march by double marches, and strike where they do not expect: that is the odd art of war.
translations.idiomatic: Pick elite troops, force-march, and surprise them—that is the way of surprise."

sentences.zh: 」穎從之。

translations.literal: " Ying followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying agreed.

sentences.zh: 及倫敗，志勸穎曰：「齊王眾號百萬，與張泓等相持不能決，大王逕得濟河，此之大勳，莫之與比，而齊王今當與大王共輔朝政。

translations.literal: When Lun fell, Zhi urged Ying, "Prince Jiong’s host claims a million men yet stalls against Zhang Hong; Your Lordship crossed the Yellow River straightway—no feat matches that, yet now Jiong expects to share power.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun’s fall Zhi urged, "Jiong’s million men are deadlocked with Zhang Hong while you crossed the river—that feat tops all—yet Jiong will demand a share of power."

sentences.zh: 志聞兩雄不俱處，功名不並立，今宜因太妃微疾，求還定省，推崇齊王，徐結四海之心，此計之上也。

translations.literal: I have heard two bulls cannot share one stall nor two names one glory; now you should plead the grand consort’s slight illness to ask leave to visit her, honor Jiong, and slowly win the realm’s hearts—that is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Two champions cannot coexist; plead your mother’s illness, return to your fief, exalt Jiong, and win the empire’s heart—that is best."

sentences.zh: 」穎納之，遂以母疾還籓，委重於冏。

translations.literal: " Ying accepted it, cited his mother’s illness to return to his fief, and piled honors on Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Ying took the advice, pleaded his mother’s illness, and left Jiong in charge.

sentences.zh: 由是穎獲四海之譽，天下歸心。

translations.literal: Thereby Ying won praise across the seas and the realm’s allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Ying thus won fame everywhere and men’s hearts turned to him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷封志為武強侯，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The court enfeoffed Zhi as marquis of Wuqiang and added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Zhi marquis of Wuqiang with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及河間王顒納李含之說，欲內除二王，樹穎儲副，遣報穎，穎將應之，志正諫，不從。

translations.literal: When Prince Yong of Hejian adopted Li Han’s plot to remove the two princes within and set Ying as heir, he informed Ying, who meant to agree; Zhi remonstrated earnestly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yong of Hejian took Li Han’s counsel to kill the two princes and make Ying heir, Ying meant to join; Zhi argued in vain.

sentences.zh: 及冏滅，穎遙執期權，遂懷觖望之心。

translations.literal: When Jiong was destroyed, Ying held long-term power from afar and nursed discontent.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell, Ying clutched power and nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 以長沙王乂在內，不得恣其所欲，密欲去乂。

translations.literal: Because Prince Yi of Changsha was in the capital and blocked his will, he secretly wished to remove Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Changsha blocked him in the capital, so he plotted secretly against Yi.

sentences.zh: 時荊州有張昌之亂，穎表求親征，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou had Zhang Chang’s rebellion; Ying memorialized to campaign in person and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rose in Jingzhou, Ying asked to lead the campaign and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 會昌等平，乃回兵以討乂。

translations.literal: When Chang was crushed, he turned the army to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Chang was crushed, he marched against Yi.

sentences.zh: 志諫曰：「公前有復皇祚之大勳，及事平，歸功於齊，辭九錫之賞，不當朝政之權，振陽翟饑人，葬黃橋白骨，皆盛德之事，四海之人莫不荷賴矣。

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated: "Your Lordship once restored the imperial house; when peace came you yielded credit to Jiong, refused the nine bestowals, stayed out of court power, fed the starving at Yangdi, and buried the dead at Huangqiao—deeds of high virtue on which the realm relied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi urged: "You restored the throne, yielded to Jiong, refused the nine gifts, stayed clear of power, fed Yangdi’s hungry, buried Huangqiao’s dead—the world owes you everything."

sentences.zh: 逆寇縱肆，猾擾荊、楚，今公掃清群難，南土以寧，振旅而旋，頓軍關外，文服入朝，此霸王者之事也。

translations.literal: Now the bandits ravage Jing and Chu; you have cleared them and pacified the south—march home in good order, camp outside the passes, and enter court in civil dress: that is a hegemon’s deed.
translations.idiomatic: Now clear the south, withdraw in good order, camp beyond the passes, and enter court in robes of peace—that is how a hegemon behaves."

sentences.zh: 」穎不納。

translations.literal: " Ying did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 及乂死，穎表志為中書監，留鄴，參署相府事。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Ying memorialized Zhi as director of the palace secretariat, left him at Ye, and had him assist the chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died Ying named Zhi palace secretariat director at Ye to run the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乘與敗于蕩陰，穎遣志督兵迎帝。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was defeated at Dangyin, Ying sent Zhi with troops to welcome the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor lost at Dangyin, Ying sent Zhi to escort him.

sentences.zh: 及王浚攻鄴，志勸穎奉天子還洛陽。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun attacked Ye, Zhi urged Ying to conduct the Son of Heaven back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun struck Ye, Zhi urged Ying to return the emperor to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時甲士尚萬五千人，志夜部分，至曉，眾皆成列，而程太妃戀鄴不欲去，穎未能決。

translations.literal: Fifteen thousand armored men remained; Zhi arrayed them through the night and by dawn they were formed, yet Grand Consort Cheng clung to Ye and Ying could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi mustered fifteen thousand men overnight, but the grand consort would not leave Ye and Ying hesitated.

sentences.zh: 俄而眾潰，唯志與子謐、兄子綝、殿中武賁千人而已，志復勸穎早發。

translations.literal: Soon the host collapsed; only Zhi, his son Mi, his nephew Shen, and a thousand palace guards remained, and Zhi again urged Ying to set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: The army melted away, leaving Zhi, his son Mi, nephew Shen, and a thousand guards; Zhi again pressed Ying to flee.

sentences.zh: 時有道士姓黃，號曰聖人，太妃信之。

translations.literal: A Daoist surnamed Huang, called the sage, had won the grand consort’s trust.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist Huang, called "the sage," had beguiled the grand consort.

sentences.zh: 及使呼人，道士求兩杯酒，飲訖，拋杯而去，於是志計始決。

translations.literal: When they summoned him he asked for two cups of wine, drank, threw down the cups, and left—only then did Zhi’s plan go forward.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist drank two cups, smashed them, and left; then Ying decided to move.

sentences.zh: 而人馬復散，志于營陣間尋索，得數乘鹿車，司馬督韓玄收集黃門，得百餘人。

translations.literal: Yet men and horses scattered again; Zhi scoured the camp and found a few deer carts; marshal Han Xuan of the guards gathered more than a hundred yellow-gate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Men and horses scattered; Zhi found deer carts while Han Xuan rounded up a hundred attendants.

sentences.zh: 志入，帝問志曰：「何故散敗至此？

translations.literal: Zhi entered; the emperor asked Zhi, "Why have we collapsed to this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi entered the presence. The emperor asked why all had fled."

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「賊去鄴尚八十里，而人士一朝駭散，太弟今欲奉陛下還洛陽。

translations.literal: " Zhi said, "The rebels are still eighty li from Ye, yet men fled in a morning panic; the heir-designate wishes to escort Your Majesty to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "The foe is still eighty li off, yet panic emptied the city; the heir-designate will escort you to Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「甚佳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Very good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」於是禦犢車便發。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they drove off in an ox cart.
translations.idiomatic: They set out at once in an ox cart.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉郝昌先領兵八千守洛陽，帝召之，至汲郡而昌至，兵仗甚盛。

translations.literal: Colonel of garrison cavalry Hao Chang had eight thousand men holding Luoyang; the emperor summoned him, and at Ji commandery Hao arrived with strong arms.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chang held Luoyang with eight thousand men; summoned, he met the train at Ji with a strong column.

sentences.zh: 志喜於復振，啟天子宜下赦書，與百姓同其休慶。

translations.literal: Zhi rejoiced at the revival and urged the Son of Heaven to issue an amnesty and share joy with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi urged a general amnesty to celebrate with the people.

sentences.zh: 既達洛陽，志啟以滿奮為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, he memorialized to name Man Fen metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he recommended Man Fen as metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 奔散者多還，百官粗備，帝悅，賜志絹二百匹、綿百斤、衣一襲、鶴綾袍一領。

translations.literal: Many who had fled returned; the hundred offices were roughly staffed again; the emperor was pleased and granted Zhi two hundred bolts of silk, a hundred jin of floss, a suit of clothes, and a crane-silk robe.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives drifted back, offices refilled, and the emperor gave Zhi silk, floss, clothes, and a crane robe.

sentences.zh: 初，河間王顒聞王浚起兵，遣右將軍張方救鄴。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince Yong of Hejian heard Wang Jun had raised troops, he sent General of the Right Zhang Fang to rescue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Yong had sent Zhang Fang to relieve Ye when Wang Jun rose.

sentences.zh: 方聞成都軍敗，頓兵洛陽，不敢進，縱兵虜掠，密欲遷都長安，將焚宗廟宮室，以絕人心。

translations.literal: Fang heard the Chengdu army had lost, halted at Luoyang, dared not advance, let his troops plunder, and secretly meant to move the capital to Chang’an, burn temples and palaces, and break men’s hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, learning of the defeat, stopped at Luoyang, plundered, and plotted to burn the capital and move west.

sentences.zh: 志說方曰：「昔董卓無道，焚燒洛陽，怨毒之聲，百年猶存，何為襲之！

translations.literal: Zhi warned Fang, "In the past Dong Zhuo’s lawless burning of Luoyang left a stench of hatred a century long—why copy him!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi told Fang, "Dong Zhuo’s arson at Luoyang is still cursed after a hundred years—do not repeat it!"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 方遂逼天子幸其壘。

translations.literal: Fang then forced the Son of Heaven to his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then compelled the emperor to enter his camp.

sentences.zh: 帝垂泣就輿，唯志侍側，曰：「陛下今日之事，當一從右將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor weeping mounted the carriage; only Zhi attended at his side and said, Your Majesty, in today's crisis you must follow the Right General in everything.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the emperor climbed into the carriage; Zhi alone stood at his side and said, Sire, you must now defer entirely to the Right General.

sentences.zh: 臣駑怯，無所雲補，唯知盡微誠，不離左右而已。

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and timid, has nothing to add, only knows to exhaust his humble loyalty and not leave your side.
translations.idiomatic: I am a dull and timid man with nothing to offer but to stay at your side with what little loyalty I have.

sentences.zh: 」停方壘三日便西，志復從至長安。

translations.literal: They halted in Fang's camp three days then went west; Zhi again followed to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After three days in Zhang Fang's camp they moved west, and Zhi followed the emperor to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 穎被黜，志亦免官。

translations.literal: When Ying was degraded, Zhi also was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying lost his rank, Zhi was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 志子諶

translations.literal: Zhi's son Chen
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son was Chen.

sentences.zh: 諶字子諒，清敏有理思，好《老》《莊》，善屬文。

translations.literal: Chen, courtesy name Ziliang, was clear, keen, and thoughtful, loved the Laozi and Zhuangzi, and excelled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, courtesy name Ziliang, was quick, lucid, fond of Daoist texts, and a fine writer.

sentences.zh: 選尚武帝女滎陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，未成禮而公主卒。

translations.literal: He was chosen to marry Emperor Wu's daughter the Princess of Xingyang, was appointed Colonel of the Household Cavalry, but before the rites were completed the princess died.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as husband to Emperor Wu's daughter, Princess of Xingyang, he was named colonel of the household cavalry, but the princess died before the wedding.

sentences.zh: 後州舉秀才，辟太尉掾。

translations.literal: Later the province raised him Flourishing Talent and summoned him as aide to the grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him flourishing talent and summoned him as aide to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 洛陽沒，隨志北依劉琨，與志俱為劉粲所虜。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, he followed Zhi north to rely on Liu Kun, and together with Zhi was taken captive by Liu Can.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he fled north with Zhi to Liu Kun and fell captive with him to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲據晉陽，留諶為參軍。

translations.literal: Can held Jinyang and kept Chen as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can held Jinyang and kept Chen on his staff.

sentences.zh: 琨收散卒，引猗盧騎還攻粲。

translations.literal: Kun gathered scattered troops and led the Youxi cavalry back to attack Can.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun rallied broken units and brought Youxi's cavalry to strike Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲敗走，諶得赴琨，先父母兄弟在平陽者，悉為劉聰所害。

translations.literal: Can fled in defeat; Chen was able to reach Kun, while parents and brothers who had been at Pingyang were all killed by Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When Can fled, Chen escaped to Kun, but every kinsman left in Pingyang had been slaughtered by Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 琨為司空，以諶為主薄，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Kun became minister of works, he made Chen chief clerk, then transferred him aide in the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kun as minister of works Chen served as chief clerk, then as bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 琨妻即諶之從母，既加親愛，又重其才地。

translations.literal: Kun's wife was Chen's aunt; she loved him as kin and also prized his talent and standing.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's wife was Chen's aunt—she loved him as family and prized his gifts.

sentences.zh: 建興末，隨琨投段匹磾。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianxing he followed Kun to join Duan Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianxing he followed Kun to Duan Pidi.

sentences.zh: 匹磾自領幽州，取諶為別駕。

translations.literal: Pidi himself held Youzhou and took Chen as senior administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Pidi took Youzhou he named Chen senior administrator.

sentences.zh: 匹磾既害琨，尋亦敗喪。

translations.literal: After Pidi murdered Kun, he too was defeated and lost.
translations.idiomatic: After Pidi killed Kun, he in turn was ruined.

sentences.zh: 時南路阻絕，段末波在遼西，諶往投之。

translations.literal: At that time the southern road was blocked; Duan Mobo was in Liaoxi, and Chen went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: With the south cut off, Chen fled to Duan Mobo in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 元帝之初，末波通使于江左，諶因其使抗表理琨，文旨甚切，於是即加弔祭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yuan, Mobo sent envoys to the lower Yangzi; Chen used their mission to submit a memorial clearing Kun's name; the wording was very cutting, whereupon the court at once sent condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan began his reign, Mobo sent envoys south; Chen rode that mission with a sharp memorial vindicating Liu Kun, and the court promptly offered rites in his honor.

sentences.zh: 累徵諶為散騎中書侍郎，而為末波所留，遂不得南渡。

translations.literal: Chen was repeatedly summoned as cavalier gentleman and palace gentleman, but Mobo detained him, so he could not cross south.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him repeatedly, but Mobo held him back from crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 末波死，弟遼代立，諶流離世故且二十載。

translations.literal: When Mobo died, his brother Dai succeeded; Chen drifted through the world's troubles for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: After Mobo died his brother Dai ruled; Chen wandered in turmoil for almost twenty years.

sentences.zh: 石季龍破遼西，復為季龍所得，以為中書侍郎、國子祭酒、侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong overran Liaoxi; Chen again fell into Jilong's hands and was made palace gentleman, libationer of the academy, palace attendant, and director of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu seized Liaoxi; Chen was taken again and given high office under the Later Zhao regime.

sentences.zh: 屬冉閔誅石氏，諶隨閔軍，于襄國遇害，時年六十七，是歲永和六年也。

translations.literal: When Ran Min slew the Shi clan, Chen followed Min's army and was killed at Xiangguo at age sixty-seven in the sixth year of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: During Ran Min's purge of the Shi family Chen followed his host and died at Xiangguo in Yonghe 6, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諶名家子，早有聲譽，才高行潔，為一時所推。

translations.literal: Chen was a son of a great house, early had fame and reputation, high talent and pure conduct, and was esteemed by his age.
translations.idiomatic: A nobleman's son famed from youth for talent and purity, he was admired by all.

sentences.zh: 值中原喪亂，與清河崔悅、穎川荀綽、河東裴憲、北地傅暢並淪陷非所，雖俱顯于石氏，恆以為辱。

translations.literal: Meeting the central plain's ruin, together with Cui Yue of Qinghe, Xun Chuo of Yingchuan, Pei Xian of Hedong, and Fu Chang of Beidi he sank into alien rule; though all were eminent under the Shi clan, they always took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the heartland fell he shared captivity with Cui Yue, Xun Chuo, Pei Xian, and Fu Chang; though they served the Shi regime they counted it disgrace.

sentences.zh: 諶每謂諸子曰：「吾身沒之後，但稱晉司空從事中郎爾。

translations.literal: Chen often told his sons, After my death only call me former aide to the Jin minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He told his sons, When I die, style me only as aide to the Jin minister of works—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」撰《祭法》，注《莊子》，及文集，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Rites of Sacrifice, annotated the Zhuangzi, and a collected works, all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Rites of Sacrifice, annotated the Zhuangzi, and left collected works that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 悅字道儒，魏司空林曾孫，劉琨妻子之侄也。

translations.literal: Yue, courtesy name Daoru, was great-grandson of Wei minister of works Cui Lin and nephew of Liu Kun's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue, courtesy name Daoru, was Cui Lin's great-grandson and nephew to Liu Kun's wife.

sentences.zh: 與諶俱為琨司空從事中郎，後為末波佐史。

translations.literal: Together with Chen he was Kun's aide in the minister of works bureau, later became scribe to Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Chen under Kun, then as scribe to Mobo.

sentences.zh: 沒石氏，亦居大官。

translations.literal: Sunk in the Shi clan, he also held high office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shi regime he too rose high.

sentences.zh: 其綽、憲、暢並別有傳。

translations.literal: As for Chuo, Xian, and Chang, each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo, Pei Xian, and Fu Chang are treated in other chapters.

sentences.zh: 華表，字偉容，平原高唐人也，父歆，清德高行，為魏太尉。

translations.literal: Hua Biao, courtesy name Weirong, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan; his father Xin had pure virtue and lofty conduct and was Wei grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Biao, courtesy name Weirong, of Gaotang in Pingyuan, was the son of Hua Xin, Wei grand commandant, a man of spotless reputation.

sentences.zh: 表年二十，拜散騎黃門郎，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: At twenty he was appointed cavalier gentleman at the yellow gates, and rose to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became cavalier at the yellow gates and rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 正元初，石苞來朝，盛稱高貴鄉公，以為魏武更生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengyuan Shi Bao came to court and loudly praised the duke of Gaoguixiang, calling him a reborn Wei Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengyuan Shi Bao attended court and hailed the duke of Gaoguixiang as Cao Cao reborn.

sentences.zh: 時聞者流汗沾背，表懼禍作，頻稱疾歸下舍，故免於大難。

translations.literal: Those who heard sweated through their backs; Biao feared disaster would arise, repeatedly claimed illness and returned to his quarters, thereby escaping great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners broke into cold sweat; Biao pleaded illness and withdrew home, escaping the worst.

sentences.zh: 後遷尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later became minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封觀陽伯。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed earl of Guanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted he was named earl of Guanyang.

sentences.zh: 坐供給喪事不整，免。

translations.literal: Because funeral supplies were not in order, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He lost office for disorderly funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，拜太子少傅，轉光祿勳。

translations.literal: In Taishi he was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, then transferred master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi he became junior tutor to the heir apparent, then master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 數歲，以老病乞骸骨。

translations.literal: After several years, because of old age and illness he begged his bones.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he asked to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「表清貞履素，有老成之美，久幹王事，靜恭匪懈。

translations.literal: An edict said, Biao is pure, chaste, and plain in conduct, with the beauty of mature steadiness; long he has labored at royal affairs, quiet and reverent without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, Biao has walked a pure, plain path and long served with quiet reverence.

sentences.zh: 而以疾固辭，章表懇至。

translations.literal: Yet because of illness he firmly declines; his memorials are earnest in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet illness makes him decline with heartfelt memorials.

sentences.zh: 今聽如所上，以為太中大夫，賜錢二十萬，床帳褥席祿賜與卿同，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Now I grant as he asked: appoint him grand counselor of the palace, grant two hundred thousand cash, bed, curtains, mats, and stipends like a minister, with a mounting-block at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He is named grand counselor of the palace with two hundred thousand cash, bedding, stipends like a minister, and a mounting-block at his gate.

sentences.zh: 」表以苦節垂名，司徒李胤、司隸王宏等並歎美表清澹退靜，以為不可得貴賤而親疏也。

translations.literal: Biao was famed for bitter integrity; Minister of Education Li Yin and metropolitan commandant Wang Hong alike praised Biao's clarity, spareness, and retirement—holding that he could not be drawn near or kept distant by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin and Wang Hong praised his spare detachment as beyond price to high or low.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年八月卒，時年七十二，諡曰康，詔賜朝服。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xianning he died, aged seventy-two, posthumous name Kang; an edict granted court robes.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianning 1, aged seventy-two, as Kang, with court robes sent posthumously.

sentences.zh: 有六子：廙、岑、嶠、鑒、澹、簡。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Yi, Cen, Qiao, Jian, Dan, and Jian—the two final names homophonous but written with different characters in the Chinese text.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Yi, Cen, Qiao, Jian, Dan, and a sixth son whose name was also pronounced Jian but written with a different character.

sentences.zh: 廙字長駿，弘敏有才義。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Changjun, was broad-minded, keen, and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Changjun, was open, quick, and able.

sentences.zh: 妻父盧毓典選，難舉姻親，故廙年三十五不得調，晚為中書通事郎。

translations.literal: His father-in-law Lu Yu headed personnel selections and shrank from raising in-laws, so Yi reached thirty-five without transfer, and late became communications gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father-in-law Lu Yu ran personnel and avoided in-law favors, Yi was not moved until thirty-five, when he became a communications gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，遷冗從僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was promoted supernumerary vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he rose to supernumerary vice-director.

sentences.zh: 少為武帝所禮，曆黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、前軍將軍、侍中、南中郎將、都督河北諸軍事。

translations.literal: From youth he was treated with respect by Emperor Wu, and held posts as gentleman at the yellow gates, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, forward general, palace attendant, south central general, and area commander of Hebei military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu favored him from youth; he rose through the yellow gates, cavalier service, forward general, palace attendant, and command on the Hebei front.

sentences.zh: 父疾篤輒還，仍遭喪舊例，葬訖復任，暠固辭，迕旨。

translations.literal: When his father was gravely ill he returned at once; by old rule after burial he should resume duty, but Yi firmly declined, defying the edict.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell mortally ill; though custom required return to office after burial, Yi refused and defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，表有賜客在鬲，使廙因縣令袁毅錄名，三客各代以奴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Biao had granted clients at Ge; he had Yi register their names with Magistrate Yuan Yi of the county—three clients each replaced by a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had registered clients at Ge through Magistrate Yuan Yi, substituting three slaves for three clients.

sentences.zh: 及毅以貨賕致罪，獄辭迷謬，不復顯以奴代客，直言送三奴與暠，而毅亦盧氏婿也。

translations.literal: When Yi was convicted for bribery, the prison testimony was confused and no longer showed the slaves-for-clients substitution, stating plainly that three slaves had been sent to Yi, and Yi was also Lu's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi fell for bribery, the indictment muddled the slave substitution and simply said three slaves were given to Hua Yi, who was also a Lu in-law.

sentences.zh: 又中書監荀勖先為中子求廙女，廙不許，為恨，因密啟帝，以袁毅貨賕者多，不可盡罪，宜責最所親者一人，因指廙當之。

translations.literal: Also, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu had earlier sought Yi's daughter for his middle son; Yi refused, and Xu bore a grudge, secretly memorializing that because many took Yuan Yi's bribes not all could be punished—the closest offender should bear blame—and pointed at Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu had wanted Yi's daughter for his son; refused, he secretly urged punishing only the chief offender and named Yi.

sentences.zh: 又綠廙有違忤之咎，遂於喪服中免暠官，削爵土。

translations.literal: Also seizing on Yi's fault of defiance, they dismissed Yi from office in mourning garb and stripped his noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped Yi of office and fief while he still mourned, citing his defiance.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚何遵奏廙免為庶人，不應襲封，請以表世孫混嗣表。

translations.literal: Grand Herald He Zun memorialized that Yi should be reduced to commoner and not inherit the title, asking that Biao's great-grandson Hun succeed Biao.
translations.idiomatic: He Zun urged reducing Yi to commoner and passing the noble title to Biao's great-grandson Hun.

sentences.zh: 有司奏曰：「廙所坐除名削爵，一時之制。

translations.literal: The responsible office memorialized, What Yi suffered—name struck and fief cut—was a temporary measure.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau replied, Yi's demotion was a provisional measure.

sentences.zh: 廙為世子，著在名簿，不聽襲嗣，此為刑罰再加。

translations.literal: Yi was registered as heir; to bar inheritance is to punish twice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recorded as heir; barring succession doubles the penalty.

sentences.zh: 諸侯犯法，八議平處者，褒功重爵也。

translations.literal: When nobles break law, the eight deliberations weigh the case to honor merit and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The eight deliberations exist to weigh noble offenders.

sentences.zh: 嫡統非犯終身棄罪，廢之為重，依律應聽襲封。

translations.literal: The main line is not cast off for life for a non-capital crime; to abolish it is harsh—by statute succession should be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: An heir-apparent should not lose succession for a non-capital fault; the law allows him to inherit.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「諸侯薨，子逾年即位，此古制也。

translations.literal: An edict said, When a noble dies, the son takes the seat after a year—such is the ancient rule.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, Heirs wait one year—that is the old rule.

sentences.zh: 應即位而廢之，爵命皆去矣，何為罪罰再加？

translations.literal: To remove him just as he should mount the throne strips rank and mandate entirely—why add a second punishment?
translations.idiomatic: To strike him as he succeeds wipes rank once—why punish twice?

sentences.zh: 且吾之責廙，以肅貪穢，本不論常法也。

translations.literal: Moreover my reproach of Yi was to frighten off corruption, not to invoke ordinary statute.
translations.idiomatic: I disciplined Yi to warn the greedy, not to apply routine law.

sentences.zh: 諸賢不能將明此意，乃更詭易禮律，不顧憲度，君命廢之，而群下復之，此為上下正相反也。

translations.literal: The worthies could not clarify this meaning, yet twist ritual and statute, heedless of the constitution—my command removed him while subordinates restored him; that makes high and low contradict each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers twisted ritual to reverse my order—high and low now contradict.

sentences.zh: 」於是有司奏免議者官，詔皆以贖論。

translations.literal: Thereupon the office memorialized to dismiss the debaters from office; an edict ordered ransom instead.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters were fined rather than dismissed.

sentences.zh: 混以世孫當受封，逃避，斷發陽狂，病喑不能語，故得不拜，世咸稱之。

translations.literal: Hun, as great-grandson, should have received the fief but fled, shaved his head, feigned madness, and fell mute, so he was not invested; the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun the great-grandson should inherit but mutilated himself and feigned madness to refuse the title, winning praise.

sentences.zh: 混字敬倫，嗣父爵，清貞簡正，歷位侍中、尚書，卒官。

translations.literal: Hun, courtesy name Jinglun, succeeded his father's rank, was pure, chaste, plain, and upright, held palace attendant and minister posts, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, courtesy name Jinglun, inherited, served as palace attendant and minister, and died in office, chaste and upright.

sentences.zh: 子陶嗣，補鞏令，沒于石勒。

translations.literal: His son Tao succeeded, was appointed magistrate of Gong, and perished under Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao succeeded, became magistrate of Gong, and died under Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 薈字敬叔，為河南尹。

translations.literal: Hui, courtesy name Jingshu, was intendant of Henan.
