translations.idiomatic: Hua Hui, courtesy name Jingshu, served as intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 與荀籓、荀組俱避賊，至臨穎，父子並遇害。

translations.literal: Together with Xun Fan and Xun Zu he fled bandits to Linying; father and son were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: With Xun Fan and Xun Zu he fled raiders to Linying and died there with his father.

sentences.zh: 廙子恆

translations.literal: Yi's son Heng
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son was Heng.

sentences.zh: 恆字敬則，博學以清素為稱。

translations.literal: Heng, courtesy name Jingze, was broadly learned and famed for purity and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, courtesy name Jingze, was learned and famed for spare purity.

sentences.zh: 尚武帝女滎陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Wu's daughter the senior princess of Xingyang and was appointed colonel of the household cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He wed Emperor Wu's elder daughter, Princess of Xingyang, and became colonel of the household cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元康初，東宮建，恆以選為太子賓友，賜爵關內侯，食邑百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang the eastern palace was founded; Heng was chosen as guest-friend to the heir apparent, enfeoffed marquis within the passes with a hundred-household fief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang, when the eastern palace opened, he was named guest-friend to the heir with a marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 辟司徒王渾倉曹掾，屬除散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、北軍中候，俄拜領軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned aide in Minister Wang Hun's granary bureau, then appointed cavalier gentleman, rising to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, north army warden, soon protector of the army with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wang Hun's staff, then rose through cavalier posts to north army warden and soon protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太常，議立郊祀。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed minister of ceremonies and debated suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of ceremonies and joined debate on suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尚書刁協、國子祭酒杜彝議，須還洛乃修郊祀。

translations.literal: Minister Diao Xie and libationer Du Yi held that sacrifice must wait for return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie and Du Yi argued suburban rites must wait on recovering Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 恆議，漢獻帝居許，即便郊柴，宜於此修立。

translations.literal: Heng argued that Emperor Xian dwelt at Xu yet sacrificed at the suburbs; rites should be set up here.
translations.idiomatic: Heng cited Emperor Xian sacrificing at Xu and urged establishing rites at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 司徒荀組、驃騎將軍王導同恆議，遂定郊祀。

translations.literal: Minister Xun Zu and general Wang Dao agreed with Heng, and suburban sacrifice was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu and Wang Dao concurred, and the suburban rite was settled.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾求解，詔曰：「太常職主宗廟，烝嘗敬重，而華恆所疾，不堪親奉職事。

translations.literal: Soon he begged relief on illness; an edict said, The minister of ceremonies presides over the temples; the autumn and spring offerings demand reverence, yet Heng's illness bars him from personally holding the duty.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave on illness; the edict said the minister of ceremonies must lead temple rites, which his health forbids.

sentences.zh: 夫子稱'吾不與祭，如不祭'，況宗伯之任職所司邪！

translations.literal: The Master said, If I do not take part in the sacrifice, it is as though there were no sacrifice—how much more the minister of rituals' charge!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said absent sacrifice is no sacrifice—how much more the minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 今轉恆為廷尉。

translations.literal: Now transfer Heng to director of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He is therefore moved to director of justice.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，加特進。

translations.literal: Before long he was added specially advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the title specially advanced.

sentences.zh: 太甯初，遷驃騎將軍，加散騎常侍，督石頭水陸諸軍事。

translations.literal: Early in Taining he was promoted general of agile cavalry with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added, commanding military affairs at Stone City by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taining he became general of agile cavalry, commanding Stone City forces.

sentences.zh: 王敦表轉恆為護軍，疾病不拜。

translations.literal: Wang Dun memorialized to transfer Heng to protector of the army; illness kept him from taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun tried to name him protector of the army, but illness blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 授金紫光祿大夫，又領太子太保。

translations.literal: He was given grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon and concurrently junior tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He received grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon and served as junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 成帝即位，加散騎常侍，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended, he added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and concurrent libationer of the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng he added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and libationer of the academy.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，以湣帝時賜爵進封一皆削除，恆更以討王敦功封苑陵縣侯，復領太常。

translations.literal: Early in Xianhe, because titles granted under Emperor Min were all annulled, Heng was re-enfeoffed marquis of Yuanling for merit against Wang Dun and again headed the ministry of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe, Min-era titles were voided; Heng was re-enfeoffed at Yuanling for merit against Wang Dun and again led the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之亂，恆侍帝左右，從至石頭，備履艱危，困悴逾年。

translations.literal: In Su Jun's rebellion Heng attended the emperor, followed to Stone City, endured every hardship, and was worn down more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's revolt he stayed with the emperor at Stone City over a year of hardship.

sentences.zh: 初，恆為州大中正，鄉人任讓輕薄無行，為恆所黜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Heng was middle appraiser for the province, townsman Ren Rang was frivolous and without conduct, and Heng degraded him.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial middle appraiser he had degraded the worthless Ren Rang.

sentences.zh: 及讓在峻軍中，任勢多所殺害，見恆輒恭敬，不肆其虐。

translations.literal: When Rang served in Jun's army and abused power to kill many, he was always reverent on seeing Heng and did not vent his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When Rang served Su Jun he spared Heng respect despite his killings.

sentences.zh: 鐘雅、劉超之死，亦將及恆，讓盡心救衛，故得免。

translations.literal: When Zhong Ya and Liu Chao died, Heng was nearly caught too, but Rang shielded him with all his heart, so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rang protected him when Zhong Ya and Liu Chao fell.

sentences.zh: 及帝加元服，又將納後。

translations.literal: When the emperor came of age and was to take an empress,
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the capping rites and chose an empress,

sentences.zh: 寇難之後，典籍靡遺，婚冠之禮，無所依據。

translations.literal: after the calamity the canons were lost and wedding and capping rites had no model.
translations.idiomatic: the war had destroyed the classics, leaving wedding and capping rites without models.

sentences.zh: 恆推尋舊典，撰定禮儀，並郊廟辟雍朝廷軌則，事並施用。

translations.literal: Heng traced old precedents, drafted ritual, and set rules for suburb, temples, ring moat, and court—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Heng recovered old texts, drafted the rituals, and set forms for suburb, temples, and court that were all adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷左光祿大夫、開府，常侍如故，固讓未拜。

translations.literal: He was promoted grand master of the left with opener of office, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary as before; he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered grand master of the left and opener of office but declined.

sentences.zh: 會卒，時年六十九，冊贈侍中、左光祿大夫、開府，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died meeting that summons, aged sixty-nine; posthumously he was given palace attendant, grand master of the left, opener of office, posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine; posthumously he received palace attendant, grand master of the left, opener of office, and the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 恆清恪儉素，雖居顯列，常布衣蔬食，年老彌篤。

translations.literal: Heng was pure, careful, spare, and plain; though he stood in high rank he always wore plain cloth and coarse food, stricter in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Though eminent he lived on coarse clothes and plain fare, stricter as he aged.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無餘財，唯有書數百卷，時人以此貴之。

translations.literal: On the day he died the house held no surplus wealth, only several hundred scrolls of books; men of the time prized him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no wealth but several hundred books, which contemporaries honored.

sentences.zh: 子俊嗣，為尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Jun succeeded and became gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hua Jun inherited the title and served as a gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 俊子仰之，大長秋。

translations.literal: Jun's son Yangzhi became grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yangzhi rose to grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 廙弟嶠

translations.literal: Yi's brother Qiao
translations.idiomatic: Yi's brother was Hua Qiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠字叔駿，才學深博，少有令聞。

translations.literal: Qiao, courtesy name Shujun, had deep and broad talent and learning, and from youth enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao, courtesy name Shujun, was famed from youth for wide learning and literary depth.

sentences.zh: 文帝為大將軍，辟為掾屬，補尚書郎，轉車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Prince Wen was grand general he summoned Qiao as staff, appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing, then transferred him aide on the left in the chariot and horse guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen took him on staff, then named him gentleman of the masters of writing and aide in the chariot guard.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was bestowed noble rank as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he received the title marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted household gentleman to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became household gentleman to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為安平太守。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Anping.

sentences.zh: 辭親老不行，更拜散騎常侍，典中書著作，領國子博士，遷侍中。

translations.literal: He declined citing aged parents and did not go; instead he was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, in charge of palace secretariat composition, concurrent libationer of the academy, then palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded aged parents and stayed home, then was named cavalier attendant-in-ordinary over secretariat writing, libationer of the academy, and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太康末，武帝頗親宴樂，又多疾病。

translations.literal: Near the end of Taikang Emperor Wu grew fond of feasts and music and often fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang Emperor Wu feasted often and was frequently ill.

sentences.zh: 屬小瘳，嶠與侍臣表賀，因微諫曰：「伏惟聖體漸就平和，上下同慶，不覺抃舞。

translations.literal: When he improved slightly, Qiao with attendant ministers memorialized congratulations and gently remonstrated, saying, "We bow that Your Sagely Person is gradually returning to peace; high and low share joy and cannot help dancing."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rallied, Qiao joined other ministers in a congratulatory memorial that gently urged restraint.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚戇，竊有微懷，以為收功於所忽，事乃無悔；

translations.literal: "We are foolish and blunt, yet privately cherish a thought: to gather merit in what is easily overlooked is to leave no regret;
translations.idiomatic: "We humbly note that guarding against small oversights prevents regret;

sentences.zh: 慮福于垂成，祚乃日新。

translations.literal: to plan blessing at the verge of completion is to renew the mandate day by day."
translations.idiomatic: securing good fortune at the moment of success keeps the mandate ever fresh."

sentences.zh: 唯願陛下深垂聖明，遠思所忽之悔，以成日新之福。

translations.literal: We only hope Your Majesty will deeply extend sagely clarity, think far on the regret of the overlooked, and complete the blessing of daily renewal."
translations.idiomatic: We pray you will ponder past slips and secure lasting good fortune."

sentences.zh: 沖靜和氣，嗇養精神，頤身于清簡之宇，留心於虛曠之域。

translations.literal: Harmonize the empty stillness and nurture the spirit, tend the person in the hall of clarity and spareness, fix the mind in the field of emptiness and distance."
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate stillness, nourish your vitality, dwell in simplicity, and keep your mind untroubled."

sentences.zh: 無厭世俗常戒，以忽群下之言，則豐慶日延，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Do not weary of the common admonitions of the world nor slight the words of your ministers—then blessings will lengthen daily and the realm will be supremely fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: Heed honest counsel and do not scorn your officials—then blessings will grow and the empire will rejoice."

sentences.zh: 」帝手詔報曰：「輒自消息，無所為慮。

translations.literal: " The emperor wrote by hand, replying, "I shall take care of myself; have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in his own hand that he would take care.

sentences.zh: 」元康初，封宣昌亭侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he was enfeoffed marquis of Xuanchang village.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he was enfeoffed marquis of Xuanchang village.

sentences.zh: 誅楊駿，改封樂鄉侯，遷尚書。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed his fief was changed to marquis of Lexiang and he was promoted minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell he was transferred to marquis of Lexiang and minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 後以嶠博聞多識，屬書典實，有良史之志，轉秘書監，加散騎常侍，班同中書。

translations.literal: Later, because Qiao was widely read and accurate in documents with the ambition of a good historian, he was transferred director of the palace library, added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with court ceremony equal to the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His erudition and archival skill won him the palace library with cavalier rank and protocol matching the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寺為內台，中書、散騎、著作及治禮音律，天文數術，南省文章，門下撰集，皆典統之。

translations.literal: The library was the inner terrace; palace secretariat, cavalier service, composition, ritual and pitch, astronomy and reckoning, southern bureau documents, and gate drafts—all fell under his oversight.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the inner archives, secretariat, ritual, astronomy, and southern bureau drafts.

sentences.zh: 初，嶠以《漢紀》煩穢，慨然有改作之意。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiao had found the Han Annals prolix and foul and harbored intent to revise them.
translations.idiomatic: He had long wished to revise the Han Annals.

sentences.zh: 會為台郎，典官制事，由是得遍觀秘笈，遂就其緒，起于光武，終於孝獻，一百九十五年，為帝紀十二卷、皇后紀二卷、十典十卷、傳七十卷及三譜、序傳、目錄，凡九十七卷。

translations.literal: When he became a terrace gentleman in charge of statutes he could read all secret books; he carried the thread from Emperor Guangwu through Emperor Xian—one hundred ninety-five years—in twelve scrolls of imperial annals, two of empresses, ten canons, seventy scrolls of biography, plus three genealogies, prefaces, and catalog: ninety-seven scrolls total.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ninety-seven scrolls from Guangwu to the last Han emperor, covering annals, empresses, canons, and biographies.

sentences.zh: 嶠以皇后配天作合，前史作外戚傳以繼末編，非其義也，故易為皇后紀，以次帝紀。

translations.literal: Qiao held that the empress, paired with Heaven, should not follow the outer kin biographies of former histories at the end; therefore he changed them to empress annals following the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced outer-kin chapters with empress annals paired to the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 又改志為典，以有《堯典》故也。

translations.literal: He also changed "treatises" to "canons" because the Yao Canon provided the model.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed treatises as canons after the Yao Canon model.

sentences.zh: 而改名《漢後書》奏之。

translations.literal: He retitled the work Later Han Annals and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his work as the Later Han Annals.

sentences.zh: 詔朝臣會議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered court ministers to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: The court convened to judge the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 時中書監荀勖、令和嶠、太常張華、侍中王濟咸以嶠文質事核，有遷固之規，實錄之風，藏之秘府。

translations.literal: Palace secretariat director Xun Xu, director He Qiao, Minister Zhang Hua, and attendant Wang Ji all held that Qiao's text was solid in matter and substance, matched Ban and Gu's plan, and had the air of true records—store it in the secret treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, He Qiao, Zhang Hua, and Wang Ji praised it as worthy of Ban Gu and ordered it sealed in the vault.

sentences.zh: 後太尉汝南王亮、司空衛瓘為東宮傅，列上通講，事遂施行。

translations.literal: Later Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan and Minister Wei Guan as eastern palace tutors jointly submitted that it be lectured throughout the court, and the matter was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: As tutors to the heir they secured imperial approval for its use at court.

sentences.zh: 嶠所著論議難駁詩賦之屬數十萬言，其所奏官制、太子宜還宮及安邊、雩祭、明堂辟雍、浚導河渠，巡禹之舊跡置都水官，修蠶宮之禮置長秋，事多施行。

translations.literal: Qiao's essays, debates, poems, and rhapsodies ran to several hundred thousand characters; his memorials on offices, the heir returning to the palace, frontier security, rain sacrifice, Bright Hall and ring moat, dredging rivers on Yu's old traces with waterworks posts, restoring silkworm rites with a grand prolonger of autumn—many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His policy papers on ritual, rivers, and the heir were often enacted.

sentences.zh: 元康三年卒，追贈少府，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Yuankang; posthumously he was given minister of the treasury, posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuankang 3 and was posthumously named minister of the treasury with the title Jian.

sentences.zh: 嶠性嗜酒，率常沈醉。

translations.literal: Qiao by nature loved wine and was often dead drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily by habit.

sentences.zh: 所撰書十典未成而終，秘書監何劭奏嶠中子徹為佐著作郎，使踵成之，未竟而卒。

translations.literal: The ten canons of his history were unfinished at his death; Director He Shao memorialized that Qiao's middle son Che be assistant compiler to finish them, but Che died before completing the work.
translations.idiomatic: His ten canons remained unfinished; He Shao asked his son Che to finish them, but Che died midway.

sentences.zh: 後監繆徵又奏嶠少子暢為佐著作郎，克成十典，並草魏、晉紀傳，與著作郎張載等俱在史官。

translations.literal: Later Director Miao Zheng memorialized that Qiao's youngest son Chang be assistant compiler; he completed the ten canons and drafted Wei and Jin annals and biographies together with compiler Zhang Zai and others in the history office.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Chang finished the canons and drafted Wei and Jin history with Zhang Zai.

sentences.zh: 永嘉喪亂，經籍遺沒，嶠書存者五十餘卷。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil the classics were lost; of Qiao's book a little over fifty scrolls survived.
translations.idiomatic: War destroyed most copies; barely fifty scrolls survived.

sentences.zh: 嶠有三子：頤、徹、暢。

translations.literal: Qiao had three sons: Yi, Che, and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yi, Che, and Chang.

sentences.zh: 頤嗣，官至長樂內史。

translations.literal: Yi succeeded; his office reached inner prefect of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi inherited and rose to inner prefect of Changle.

sentences.zh: 暢有才思，所著文章數萬言。

translations.literal: Chang had literary talent; his writings ran to several tens of thousands of characters.
translations.idiomatic: Chang wrote extensively.

sentences.zh: 遭寇亂，避難荊州，為賊所害，時年四十。

translations.literal: Meeting bandit turmoil he fled to Jingzhou and was killed by bandits at age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Jingzhou and died at forty at bandit hands.

sentences.zh: 石鑒，字林伯，樂陵厭次人也。

translations.literal: Shi Jian, courtesy name Linbo, was a man of Yanci in Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian, courtesy name Linbo, came from Yanci in Leling commandery.

sentences.zh: 出自寒素，雅志公亮。

translations.literal: He rose from cold and plain families, yet his aim was public and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Of humble origin, he aimed at upright public service.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，曆尚書郎、侍御史、尚書左丞、御史中丞，多所糾正，朝廷憚之，出為并州刺史、假節、護匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: Serving Wei he held posts as gentleman of the masters of writing, attendant censor, left assistant in the masters of writing, and palace assistant secretary, correcting much; the court feared him, and he went out as inspector of Bing province with credential staff and protector of the Xiongnu middle rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he rose through secretariat and censor posts, awed the court with rectitude, and became inspector of Bing with border command.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封堂陽子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed viscount of Tangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin he was enfeoffed viscount of Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 入為司隸校尉，轉尚書。

translations.literal: He entered as metropolitan commandant, then minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as metropolitan commandant, then minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時秦、涼為虜所敗，遣鑒都督隴右諸軍事，坐論功虛偽免官。

translations.literal: When Qin and Liang were defeated by tribes he was sent as area commander of Longyou military affairs and dismissed for false merit claims.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded on the Longyou front but lost office for inflated battle claims.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮南將軍、豫州刺史，坐討吳賊虛張首級。

translations.literal: Later he was general who guards the south and inspector of Yu province, convicted for inflating heads in the Wu campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Later as southern commander he again inflated enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔雲中守魏尚以斬首不實受刑，武牙將軍田順以詐增虜獲自殺，誣罔敗法，古今所疾。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Long ago Yunzhong governor Wei Shang was punished for false head counts, and general Tian Shun of the martial fangs killed himself for lying about captives—deceit that ruins law is hated in every age."
translations.idiomatic: The edict cited Wei Shang and Tian Shun punished for false battle claims.

sentences.zh: 鑒備大臣，吾所取信。

translations.literal: Jian is a great minister in whom I place trust.
translations.idiomatic: Jian is a chief minister I trusted.

sentences.zh: 往者西事，公欺朝廷，以敗為得，竟不推究。

translations.literal: In the western affair you deceived the court, calling defeat victory, yet it was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign you lied to the throne yet went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 中間黜免未久，尋復授用，冀能補過，而乃與下同詐。

translations.literal: Shortly after dismissal you were reused, hoping you would mend faults, yet you again conspired with subordinates in fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to office, you again cheated with your staff.

sentences.zh: 所謂大臣，義得爾乎！

translations.literal: Is this how a great minister should behave?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this conduct fit for a great minister?

sentences.zh: 有司奏是也，顧未忍耳。

translations.literal: The office memorialized agreement; I have not yet had the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau agreed to harsh punishment, but I stayed my hand.

sentences.zh: 今遣歸田里，終身不得復用，勿削爵土也。

translations.literal: Now send him home to the fields, never to be employed again—do not strip his noble rank and fief."
translations.idiomatic: He is banished for life from office but keeps his title and land.

sentences.zh: 」久之，拜光祿勳，復為司隸校尉，稍加特進，遷右光祿大夫、開府，領司徒。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed master of ceremonies, again metropolitan commandant, gradually added specially advanced, promoted grand master of the right with opener of office, concurrent minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he returned as master of ceremonies, metropolitan commandant, grand master of the right, and minister of education.

sentences.zh: 前代三公冊拜，皆設小會，所以崇宰輔之制也。

translations.literal: Formerly the three dukes on investiture held small feasts to honor the chancellor's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient three-ducal investitures included a modest banquet to honor the office.

sentences.zh: 自魏末已後，廢不復行。

translations.literal: From late Wei onward it was abandoned and not revived.
translations.idiomatic: Late Wei had dropped the custom.

sentences.zh: 至鑒，有詔令會，遂以為常。

translations.literal: When Jian received appointment an edict ordered the feast, and thereafter it became regular.
translations.idiomatic: For Jian the court revived the banquet and made it precedent.

sentences.zh: 太康末，拜司空，領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Near the end of Taikang he was appointed minister of works and concurrent grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he became minister of works and grand tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，鑒與中護軍張劭監統山陵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died Jian with central protector Zhang Shao supervised the mausoleum works.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu's death he and Zhang Shao oversaw the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 時大司馬、汝南王亮為太傅楊駿所疑，不敢臨喪，出營城外。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Marshal Prince Liang of Runan was suspected by Grand Tutor Yang Jun and dared not attend mourning, camping outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang feared Yang Jun and stayed outside the city during the funeral.

sentences.zh: 時有告亮欲舉兵討駿，駿大懼，白太后令帝為手詔，詔鑒及張劭使率陵兵討亮。

translations.literal: Someone reported Liang meant to raise troops against Jun; Jun was terrified and told the empress dowager to have the emperor issue a handwritten edict ordering Jian and Zhang Shao to lead tomb guards against Liang.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor drove Yang Jun to order Jian and Zhang Shao to attack Prince Liang with tomb guards.

sentences.zh: 劭，駿甥也，便率所領催鑒速發，鑒以為不然，保持之，遣人密覘視亮，已別道還許昌，於是駿止，論者稱之。

translations.literal: Shao was Jun's nephew and urged Jian to march at once; Jian thought it wrong, held back, secretly watched Liang, and found he had already returned to Xuchang by another road—Jun then stopped; commentators praised Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao pressed for immediate attack; Jian delayed, reconnoitered, and proved Liang had left for Xuchang—Jun canceled the order and men praised Jian.

sentences.zh: 山陵訖，封昌安縣侯。

translations.literal: When the mausoleum was finished he was enfeffed marquis of Chang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: After the tomb work he was enfeoffed marquis of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 元康初，為太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he became grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he was grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，克壯慷慨，自遇若少年，時人美之。

translations.literal: Past eighty he was still hale and ardent, comporting himself like a youth; men of the time admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty he remained vigorous and was admired.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Shortly he died, posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died with posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子陋，字處賤，襲封，曆屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: His son Lou, courtesy name Chujian, inherited the fief and held posts up to colonel of garrison cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lou inherited and rose to colonel of garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 先是，張華被誅，冏建議欲復其官爵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Hua was executed, Prince Jiong proposed restoring his titles and fief.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Hua was executed, Prince Jiong moved to restore his honors.

sentences.zh: 論者或以為非，羨駁之曰：「自天子已下，爭臣各有差，不得歸罪於一人也。

translations.literal: Some debaters opposed it; Wen Xian refuted them, saying, "From the Son of Heaven down each remonstrating officer has his grade—guilt cannot be pinned on one man alone."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xian argued guilt cannot rest on one minister alone.

sentences.zh: 故晏子曰：'為已死亡，非其親昵，誰能任之？

translations.literal: Therefore Yanzi said, "When a man dies for his lord, unless they are kin, who will answer for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying said none but kin answer for the dead.

sentences.zh: 」裏克之殺二庶，陳乞之立陽生，漢朝之誅諸呂，皆積年之後乃得立事。

translations.literal: The killing of the two heirs by Li Ke, the setting up of Yangsheng by Chen Qi, and Han's slaughter of the Lü clan all came to pass only after years.
translations.idiomatic: Historical precedents like Li Ke and the Lü purge unfolded over years.

sentences.zh: 未有事主見存，而得行其志於數月之內者也。

translations.literal: Never has a ruler still lived while a minister carried out such a design within months.
translations.idiomatic: No minister executes such a plan in mere months while the ruler lives.

sentences.zh: 式乾之會，張華獨諫。

translations.literal: At the Shi Qian meeting Zhang Hua alone remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shi Qian affair Zhang Hua alone remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 上宰不和，不能承風贊善，望其指麾從命，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: The chief ministers were not at peace and could not second wise counsel; to expect him to wave a banner and obey orders was hard indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers were divided; expecting Hua to command alone was impossible.

sentences.zh: 況今皇后譖害其子，內難不預，禮非所在。

translations.literal: Moreover the empress now slandered and harmed her son; he did not foresee inner strife—ritual did not require it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress harmed her son; Hua could not have foreseen inner court murder.

sentences.zh: 且後體齊於帝，尊同皇極，罪在枉子，事不為逆，義非所討。

translations.literal: The empress matches the emperor in body; she shares the supreme pole—guilt lay in a wrongful son, not rebellion, and justice does not demand her execution.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ranked with the emperor; fault lay with the prince, not treason.

sentences.zh: 今以華不能廢枉子之後，與趙盾不討殺君之賊同，而貶責之，於義不經通也。

translations.literal: Now to fault Hua for not deposing the son after the empress's crime, equating him with Zhao Dun who failed to punish his lord's killer, is unjust."
translations.idiomatic: Blaming Hua like Zhao Dun for failing to punish the empress twists justice.

sentences.zh: 」華竟得追復爵位。

translations.literal: " Zhang Hua's noble rank was restored in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 其後以從駕討成都王穎有勳，封大陵縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: Later, for merit following the carriage in punishing Prince Ying of Chengdu, he was enfeoffed duke of Daling with one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the duchy of Daling for the campaign against Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，加後將軍，范陽王虓敗於許昌也，自牧冀州，羨乃避之。

translations.literal: He went out as inspector of Ji province, added rear general; when Prince Xiao of Fanyang was defeated at Xuchang and seized Ji province himself, Xian yielded.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji inspector he stepped aside when Prince Xiao of Fanyang took the province after his defeat at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之幸長安，以羨為中書令，不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui fled to Changan Xian was named director of the palace secretariat but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled west he was named palace secretariat director but declined.

sentences.zh: 及帝還洛陽，徵為中書監，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Luoyang he was summoned as palace secretariat director with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled at Luoyang he was offered palace secretariat director with cavalier rank.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會帝崩。

translations.literal: Before investiture the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: He had not taken office when the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，遷左光祿大夫、開府，領司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended he was promoted grand master of the left with opener of office, concurrent minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he became grand master of the left and minister of education.

sentences.zh: 論者僉謂為速。

translations.literal: Critics all said the rise was too fast.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called his promotion hasty.

sentences.zh: 在位未幾，病卒，贈司徒，諡曰元。

translations.literal: He held office briefly, then died of illness; posthumously he was minister of education, posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after with posthumous honors as minister of education, title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有三子：祗、允、裕。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Zhi, Yun, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhi, Yun, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 祗字敬齊，太傅西曹掾。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Jingqi, was aide in the western bureau of the grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Jingqi, served the grand tutor's western bureau.

sentences.zh: 允字敬咸，太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yun, courtesy name Jingxian, was household gentleman to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, courtesy name Jingxian, was household gentleman to the heir.

sentences.zh: 裕字敬嗣，尚武安長公主，官至左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Jingsi, married the senior princess of Wu'an and rose to grand master of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Jingsi, married the senior princess of Wu'an and reached grand master of the left.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏中朝，承累世之資，建兼併之業，衣冠斯盛，英彥如林。

translations.literal: The historian says: Mid-Jin inherited many generations' capital and pursued annexing enterprise; caps and sashes flourished and heroes stood thick as a forest.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say mid-Jin inherited wealth and ambition; talent filled the court.

sentences.zh: 此數公者，或以雅望處台槐，或以高名居保傅，自非一時之秀，亦曷能至於斯。

translations.literal: These several men—some by pure repute held the locust terrace, some by high name tutored the heir—unless they were outstanding of their time, how could they reach such heights?
translations.idiomatic: These men reached the highest posts only as exceptional talents of their day.

sentences.zh: 惜其參緘於論道之辰，獨善於兼濟之日，良圖鯁議，無足多談。

translations.literal: It is a pity that in hours meant for counsel they kept private virtue instead of aiding all; fine plans and blunt speech need not be multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in crisis they often chose private safety over saving the realm—little more need be said.

sentences.zh: 然退已進賢，林叔弘推讓之美；

translations.literal: Yet yielding place to lift the worthy shows Linshu's beauty of deference;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao's yielding set a standard of deference;

sentences.zh: 自家刑國，宣伯協恭孝之規。

translations.literal: regulating self to order the state shows Xuanbo's model of filial harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin harmonized family and state in filial duty;

sentences.zh: 子若之儒素為基，偉容之苦節流譽，慶垂來葉，不亦宜哉！

translations.literal: Ziruo's Confucian plainness as foundation, Weirong's bitter integrity winning fame—blessings reaching later leaves: was it not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin's scholarship and Hua Biao's austerity left blessings for posterity—fitting praise.

sentences.zh: 石鑒以公亮升，溫羨以明寤顯，屬於危亂，不隕其名。

translations.literal: Shi Jian rose by public brightness; Wen Xian shone by keen insight; amid peril they did not lose their names.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian and Wen Xian kept their reputations through turmoil.

sentences.zh: 歲寒見松柏之後凋，斯人之謂矣。

translations.literal: Only when the year is cold do we see the pine and cypress last wither—such were these men.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, winter reveals the evergreen—so with these men.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：讓矣密陵，孝哉廣陸。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yielding was the lord of Miling; filial was the lord of Guanglu.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: yielding Zheng Mao, filial Zheng Mo;

sentences.zh: 欽既博雅，表亦貞肅。

translations.literal: Qin was broad and learned; Biao was chaste and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin was learned and pure; Hua Biao was stern and true.

sentences.zh: 鑒績克宣，溫聲載穆。

translations.literal: Jian's deeds were able to be proclaimed; Wen's voice carried solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian's deeds shone abroad, and Wen Xian's name carried a quiet dignity.

sentences.zh: 同鏘玉振，爭芬蘭鬱。

translations.literal: Together they clanged like jade sounding; they vied in fragrance like orchid luxuriance.
translations.idiomatic: Together they chimed like struck jade and rivaled the orchid's scent—men of a piece with the finest company.
